findings.passage: Photo identification is required for almost everything from buying alcohol to flying on a plane.  Voting is a privilege of being an US citizen, and should be limited to only those who are eligible to vote and can prove so by government issued photo ID.
findings.note: Candidate's own questionnaire answer, given when she was a first-time candidate for the House seat; the page's default view is the May 17, 2022 primary race and lists later races too, so the exact answer date is not printed beside the text. She explains why photo ID should be required to vote and ties voting to citizenship.

findings.passage: I would like to limit the number of days of early voting to no more than a week; you must request an absentee ballot and have signature/photo verification to cast a vote if you are not available/unable to vote in person on regular voting days.
findings.note: Same questionnaire, answer to what laws she would propose on voting practices. She names signature or photo verification for absentee ballots and a short early-voting window.
subjects: photo ID for absentee or mail ballots

findings.passage: Return to paper ballots, and remove any cellular modem and  any connectivity of the internet to the voting machines.  Require government issued photo ID.  Eliminate drop boxes, and ballot harvesting.
findings.note: Same answer, continued: paper ballots, disconnected machines, government-issued photo ID, no drop boxes, no ballot harvesting.
subjects: voting machine connectivity and paper ballots
